lens: The evidence pool lacks direct data on retatrutide triple agonists, forcing reliance on adjacent incretin literature to frame gaps in lean mass dynamics and cardioprotection for triple agonists, which is too narrow for a publishable thesis without new extractions.
known_to_ignore: Tirzepatide demonstrates up to 22.5% weight loss in phase 3 obesity trials
Semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly yields 15-17% mean weight loss with cardioprotection
Incretin-based therapies commonly cause ∼10% lean mass loss
Incretin-based therapies achieve ≥5% body weight reduction in half of patients
tensions: Contradiction between weight loss therapies inducing lean mass loss (e.g., ∼10% loss) and those potentially increasing lean mass (e.g., ∼3 kg gain) in different studies
Variation in cardiovascular risk reduction efficacy across incretin agents, with semaglutide showing MACE reduction in SELECT trial but unverified for triple agonists
gaps: Absence of direct clinical trial data on retatrutide's effects on lean mass preservation or loss
Lack of comparative analysis between retatrutide triple agonists and dual agonists like tirzepatide on body composition outcomes
Unexplored cardioprotective effects of retatrutide in obesity populations beyond T2D
reviewer_objections: No primary evidence on retatrutide is cited, making all extrapolations from other drugs speculative and unsubstantiated
The focus on lean mass changes ignores potential dose-specific effects or long-term safety data for retatrutide
Adjacent literature on dual agonists may not translate to triple agonist mechanisms, limiting generalizability
next_extractions: Phase 3 clinical trial data for retatrutide on percentage weight loss and lean mass changes, especially in subgroups with obesity
Head-to-head studies comparing retatrutide with tirzepatide and semaglutide on cardiovascular outcomes and body composition
Dose-response relationships for retatrutide in terms of strength gains or preservation, inspired by hints on ∼25% strength increases
